capabilities: Sync vault changes across devices in real time with a status-bar indicator
Encrypt all files on-device with AES-256-GCM before upload so the server stores only ciphertext
Configure per-device attachment types, config-folder sync, and folder exclusions
Browse file version history, restore deleted files, and resolve sync conflicts
Self-host the server via Docker and manage users, invite codes, groups, and storage in an admin UI
extras: The README notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff, warns that the vault password is unrecoverable from the server, and documents extensive self-hosting troubleshooting (reverse proxy, presigned S3 URLs, AVX2 baseline builds). Docs are bilingual (Korean/English).
problem: Obsidian's built-in Sync relies on the vendor's service and pricing, and plain file-sync solutions lack zero-knowledge encryption, version history, and conflict handling.

relations.evidence: the plugin uploads/downloads encrypted blobs directly to MinIO, bypassing the API
Configure the Telegram notification integration (bot token + chat ID, with a test button)

summary: Self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted vault sync that syncs your vault across devices through a Docker-based server you run yourself.
